mcqs.question: Isomerism is best defined as:

options.A: Compounds having the same molecular formula but different connectivity or spatial arrangement
options.B: Compounds having different molecular formulas but the same functional group
options.C: Compounds that differ only in the number of carbon atoms
options.D: Compounds that have identical structures and properties

mcqs.answer: Compounds having the same molecular formula but different connectivity or spatial arrangement
mcqs.explanation: Isomerism refers to compounds that possess the same molecular formula yet differ either in the way atoms are connected (structural isomerism) or in their three‑dimensional arrangement (stereoisomerism). Options B, C and D describe unrelated concepts.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly describes structural isomerism?

options.A: Isomers have the same connectivity but differ in spatial arrangement around a double bond
options.B: Isomers have the same molecular formula but differ in the order in which atoms are bonded
options.C: Isomers have different molecular formulas but identical physical properties
options.D: Isomers differ only in the number of chiral centers present

mcqs.answer: Isomers have the same molecular formula but differ in the order in which atoms are bonded
mcqs.explanation: Structural (or constitutional) isomerism arises when compounds share a molecular formula but the atoms are linked in different sequences, giving distinct structures. Option A describes stereoisomerism, C is incorrect because molecular formulas are the same, and D refers to a specific type of stereoisomerism (enantiomerism).

mcqs.question: Chain isomerism refers to:

options.A: Isomers that differ in the position of a functional group on the same carbon skeleton
options.B: Isomers that have different carbon skeletons (different branching) but the same molecular formula
options.C: Isomers that differ only in the arrangement around a double bond
options.D: Isomers that possess the same functional group but belong to different families

mcqs.answer: Isomers that have different carbon skeletons (different branching) but the same molecular formula
mcqs.explanation: Chain isomerism is a type of structural isomerism where the carbon chain is rearranged – for example, n‑butane and isobutane. Option A describes position isomerism, C describes geometric (cis‑trans) isomerism, and D describes functional isomerism.

mcqs.question: Which pair of compounds best illustrates position isomerism?
mcqs.explanation: Position isomerism occurs when the functional group is attached to different carbon atoms of the same skeleton. 1‑Butanol (‑OH on C‑1) and 2‑Butanol (‑OH on C‑2) are classic examples. Option A is chain isomerism, C is geometric (cis‑trans) isomerism, and D is functional isomerism.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs of compounds are functional isomers?
mcqs.explanation: Functional isomerism involves compounds with the same molecular formula but belonging to different functional groups. Ethanol (an alcohol) and dimethyl ether (an ether) both have formula C₂H₆O, making them functional isomers. Option A differs in degree of unsaturation, B is geometric isomerism, and D is chain isomerism.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand stereoisomerism at the required level
mcqs.question: Compound X and Compound Y have the same molecular formula and the same connectivity, but differ in the spatial arrangement of groups around a C=C double bond. Which type of isomerism does this represent?
mcqs.explanation: When two compounds differ only in the relative positions of substituents around a double bond, they are geometric (cis‑trans) isomers, a subclass of stereoisomerism. Chain and position isomerism involve connectivity changes, while functional isomerism involves different functional groups.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements is **incorrect** about isomerism?

options.A: Isomers always have the same molecular formula.
options.B: Isomers may differ in physical properties such as boiling point.
options.C: All isomers have identical chemical reactivity.
options.D: Isomerism includes both structural and stereoisomerism.

mcqs.answer: All isomers have identical chemical reactivity.
mcqs.explanation: While isomers share a molecular formula, their different structures or spatial arrangements often lead to different chemical reactivities. Hence statement C is false. Statements A, B, and D are correct descriptions of isomerism.

mcqs.question: If two compounds C₅H₁₂ have the same molecular formula but one is a straight‑chain alkane and the other has a branched chain, what can be inferred about their physical properties?

options.A: Both will have identical boiling points because they have the same formula.
options.B: The branched isomer will generally have a lower boiling point than the straight‑chain isomer.
options.C: The straight‑chain isomer will have a lower melting point than the branched isomer.
options.D: Both will be gases at room temperature.

mcqs.answer: The branched isomer will generally have a lower boiling point than the straight‑chain isomer.
mcqs.explanation: Branching reduces the surface area, weakening London dispersion forces, so branched alkanes usually boil at lower temperatures than their straight‑chain counterparts. Option A ignores the effect of shape, C reverses the typical trend, and D is incorrect because C₅H₁₂ compounds are liquids at room temperature.
